title: Testing Python Code Quiz
description: Practice assert, pytest, and the unittest module for automated checks.

questions.prompt: pytest discovers test functions whose names start with test_.
questions.explanation: By default pytest collects functions like test_add() in test_*.py files.

questions.prompt: What does assert x == 5 do in a test?
options: Passes if the expression is true, otherwise raises AssertionError
questions.explanation: assert is the simplest check; pytest rewrites asserts for clearer failures.

questions.prompt: Which command often runs pytest in a project?
questions.explanation: After installing pytest, run pytest from the project root.

questions.prompt: Why write automated tests?
questions.explanation: Tests document expected behavior and fail when bugs return.

questions.prompt: unittest is in the Python standard library.
questions.explanation: import unittest works without pip install.

questions.prompt: A test file named test_math.py is a common pytest convention because:
options: pytest finds files matching test_*.py or *_test.py by default
questions.explanation: Naming conventions help tools discover tests automatically.

questions.prompt: unittest.TestCase methods often start with:
questions.explanation: The unittest runner collects test* methods on TestCase subclasses.

questions.prompt: self.assertEqual(a, b) in unittest checks:
options: That a and b are equal, failing the test if not
That a is a file path
questions.explanation: TestCase provides many assert* helpers similar to plain assert.

questions.prompt: Tests should be small and check one behavior when possible.
questions.explanation: Focused tests make failures easier to diagnose.

questions.prompt: Running tests before a commit helps you:
options: Verify changes did not break existing behavior
questions.explanation: Fast feedback loops are a core developer habit.

questions.prompt: pytest -q typically means:
questions.explanation: Flags adjust verbosity and reporting style.

questions.prompt: A failing test output usually shows:
options: Which test failed and how actual differed from expected
questions.explanation: Good runners highlight the assertion that failed.

questions.prompt: You can test functions that raise exceptions with pytest.raises.
questions.explanation: Expected errors are part of correct behavior for invalid input.

questions.prompt: Arrange-Act-Assert describes:
options: Set up data, run code, check the result
questions.explanation: Clear test structure improves readability.

questions.prompt: Compared to manual clicking, automated tests are:
options: Repeatable and fast on every change
Always slower than shipping without tests
questions.explanation: Automation scales as the project grows.

questions.prompt: if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main() is used to:
options: Run unittest tests when the file is executed directly
questions.explanation: The guard keeps tests from running on import.

questions.prompt: Test code lives in separate files or modules from production code in most projects.
questions.explanation: Keeping tests apart avoids shipping test helpers in the app.

questions.prompt: A regression is:
options: Old behavior breaking after a new change
questions.explanation: Tests exist partly to prevent regressions.

questions.prompt: assert 1 + 1 == 2 in a script (not pytest) will:
options: Do nothing if true; raise AssertionError if false
questions.explanation: Plain assert works outside test runners too.

questions.prompt: Good first tests for a function usually cover:
options: Typical input and at least one edge case
questions.explanation: Start with happy path plus one failure or boundary case.
